name: Intra-node NVLink latency is ~10x lower than inter-node InfiniBand latency, dictating TP vs PP placement
symptom: Tensor-parallel sharding across a node boundary (using InfiniBand instead of NVLink) incurs ~10x higher latency per collective operation, which can dominate inference time for small-batch or low-latency workloads.
root_cause: NVLink provides ~25 GB/s per link per direction with sub-microsecond latency (the physical link is on the same board or backplane). InfiniBand NDR provides 50 GB/s per port per direction but with ~1-2 microsecond latency due to the network interface card, switch hops, and protocol processing. The latency difference is approximately 10x. For tensor-parallel, every layer boundary requires an all-reduce, so the latency penalty is paid per layer. For pipeline-parallel, communication happens only at stage boundaries, so the latency penalty is amortized over a full pipeline stage.
workaround: Keep tensor-parallel groups within a single node (8 GPUs with NVSwitch) to use NVLink. Use pipeline-parallel across nodes to minimize the number of inter-node collectives. For MoE models, use expert-parallel within a node if possible. The general rule: TP within node, PP across nodes, DP across nodes.
notes: This is the fundamental reason the 8-GPU node exists as a unit of scaling. The 10x latency gap means that a TP=8 configuration across 2 nodes (4 GPUs each) will be significantly slower than TP=8 within a single node, even if the aggregate bandwidth is similar. The exact latency numbers depend on the specific hardware and NCCL version, but the order-of-magnitude difference is consistent across generations.
